rv.q: By the time the show reaches its toe-tapping, feel-good conclusion, the audience are on their feet and dancing again, cheering and cheered as panto’s inimitable energy lends them much-needed warmth and enjoyment in the coldest season of the year.
The Stratford East panto is, even in its weakest years, a highlight of the festive season, and Robin Hood and the Merry Mandem is magnificent even by this high standard.

Too simplistic for adults to enjoy as a comedy, yet perhaps too modernised and moralistic to resonate with younger audiences, it falls into an uncomfortable middle ground between a traditional family pantomime and an adult show.
Original, stylish, inclusive, politically cheeky and tremendously entertaining, this is everything a modern pantomime should be.

cn.t: Critics are largely won over by this vibrant East London panto, praising its sharp political satire and infectious energy. One dissenter finds it struggles to define its audience, but the consensus leans strongly positive.
